concepts.def: A community of organisms together with their physical environment.
Shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
Makes its own food by photosynthesis; the start of a food chain.
Breaks down dead matter, recycling nutrients.
Interlinked food chains showing feeding relationships.
Recycles carbon via respiration, photosynthesis, combustion and decay.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecological Relationships — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecological Relationships brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecological Relationships.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In a food chain, the arrows show the direction of:
options: energy transfer
predator movement
water flow
carbon dioxide release

mcqs.q: Most energy is lost between trophic levels mainly through:
options: respiration and heat loss
photosynthesis
absorption of minerals
reflection of light
estimate the number of organisms in an area by sampling
measure the temperature of a habitat
trap small mammals overnight
weigh individual plants

mcqs.q: Decomposers are important in an ecosystem because they:
options: recycle nutrients from dead material
produce food by photosynthesis
are the top predators
reflect sunlight onto plants

mcqs.q: What do the arrows in a food chain represent?
options: Decomposers make their own food by photosynthesis.
The arrows show which animals live together.
The arrows show the direction of energy transfer, pointing from the organism eaten to the one that eats it.
The arrows point toward the animal that gets eaten.

mcqs.q: Why are there usually fewer top predators than producers?
options: Energy is lost at each trophic level, so less energy is available to support fewer organisms higher up the chain.
There are fewer predators simply because they are bigger animals.
There are fewer predators only because they reproduce slowly.
Decomposers make their own food by photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: What is the role of decomposers?
options: Decomposers make their own food by photosynthesis.
The arrows show which animals live together.
Decomposers are the top predators in the food chain.
Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste, releasing nutrients back into the soil for plants to reuse.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Pyramid of biomass”?
options: A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer.
A square frame of known area used to sample the number or percentage cover of organisms so a population size can be estimated.
A sequence showing the flow of energy from a producer to consumers, with arrows pointing in the direction in which energy is transferred.
A diagram showing the dry mass of organisms at each trophic level, usually decreasing from producers upwards.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Decomposer”?
options: A square frame of known area used to sample the number or percentage cover of organisms so a population size can be estimated.
A diagram showing the dry mass of organisms at each trophic level, usually decreasing from producers upwards.
An organism, usually a green plant, that makes its own food by photosynthesis and forms the start of a food chain.
An organism such as a bacterium or fungus that breaks down dead organisms and waste, recycling nutrients into the ecosystem.
